points.title: 童年时光
points.description: 马尔克斯出生于哥伦比亚北部小镇阿拉卡塔卡，由外祖父母抚养长大。这段童年经历深刻影响了他后来的文学创作，尤其是《百年孤独》中的马孔多小镇原型。外祖母讲述的民间传说和家族故事成为他魔幻现实主义风格的源头。在这段时间，他接触了拉丁美洲丰富的民间文化和传统，这些元素后来融入他的作品中，形成了独特的叙事风格。
points.descriptionEn: Born in Aracataca, Colombia, García Márquez was raised by his grandparents. This childhood profoundly influenced his later literary work, particularly the fictional town of Macondo in 'One Hundred Years of Solitude.' The folk tales and family stories told by his grandmother became the source of his magical realism style. During this period, he absorbed the rich folk culture and traditions of Latin America, which later merged into his works, forming a unique narrative style.

points.title: 新闻与文学起步
points.description: 马尔克斯在波哥大国立大学学习法律，但很快转向新闻工作。他担任《观察家报》记者，期间报道了多次政治事件和社会问题。1955年，他因揭露海军军官贿赂事件被迫流亡国外。这段经历让他深刻认识到拉丁美洲的政治腐败和社会不公，这些主题成为他后来作品的重要元素。在波哥大，他开始创作短篇小说，形成了自己独特的叙事风格，并结识了多位重要文学人物。
points.descriptionEn: García Márquez studied law at the National University of Bogotá but quickly shifted to journalism. He worked as a reporter for 'El Espectador,' covering numerous political events and social issues. In 1955, he was forced into exile abroad after exposing a naval officer bribery scandal. This experience gave him profound insight into Latin America's political corruption and social injustice, themes that became central to his later works. In Bogotá, he began writing short stories, developing his unique narrative style and meeting important literary figures.

points.title: 欧洲流亡
points.description: 流亡期间，马尔克斯在巴黎生活和工作，与拉丁美洲其他流亡作家如胡利奥·科塔萨尔等人交往密切。这段时期他经历了经济困难，但也获得了创作自由。他在巴黎完成了短篇小说集《没有人给他写信的上校》等早期作品。欧洲的经历让他接触到现代主义文学和欧洲文化，同时加深了他对拉丁美洲身份的思考。这段流亡生活为他后来的魔幻现实主义风格提供了更广阔的视野和更深刻的思考。
points.descriptionEn: During his exile, García Márquez lived and worked in Paris, associating closely with other Latin American exiled writers like Julio Cortázar. This period was marked by financial difficulties but also afforded him creative freedom. In Paris, he completed early works such as the short story collection 'No One Writes to the Colonel.' His European exposure to modernist literature and European culture, combined with deepened reflection on his Latin American identity, provided a broader perspective and deeper thought for his later magical realism style.

points.title: 记者与作家
points.description: 马尔克斯移居委内瑞拉加拉加斯，担任《委内瑞拉画报》编辑。这一时期他继续从事新闻工作，同时进行文学创作。1962年，他发表小说《恶时辰》，获得重要文学奖项。在加拉加斯，他完成了《百年孤独》的初稿，但多次修改后才最终出版。这段时间他深入研究了拉丁美洲的历史和政治，为魔幻现实主义风格的形成奠定了基础。加拉加斯时期是他从记者向全职作家转变的关键阶段。
points.descriptionEn: García Márquez moved to Caracas, Venezuela, where he worked as an editor for 'Momento' magazine. During this period, he continued his journalistic work while pursuing literary创作. In 1962, he published the novel 'Bad Season' and received significant literary awards. In Caracas, he completed the first draft of 'One Hundred Years of Solitude,' though it underwent multiple revisions before final publication. This time saw him deeply studying Latin American history and politics, laying the foundation for his magical realism style. The Caracas period marked his crucial transition from journalist to full-time writer.

points.title: 文学巅峰
points.description: 1967年，马尔克斯在墨西哥城出版了《百年孤独》，这部作品使他一举成名，成为魔幻现实主义文学的代表作。在墨西哥城，他创作了多部重要作品，包括《家长的没落》《霍乱时期的爱情》等。这一时期他积极参与拉丁美洲的政治活动，支持古巴革命和尼加拉瓜桑地诺民族解放阵线。墨西哥城成为他文学创作和政治活动的中心，他的作品被翻译成多种语言，影响遍及全球。1972年，他获得纽斯塔特国际文学奖，1982年获得诺贝尔文学奖。
points.descriptionEn: In 1967, García Márquez published 'One Hundred Years of Solitude' in Mexico City, which brought him immediate fame and became the representative work of magical realism. In Mexico City, he wrote several major works including 'The Autumn of the Patriarch' and 'Love in the Time of Cholera.' During this period, he actively participated in Latin American politics, supporting the Cuban Revolution and the Nicaraguan Sandinista National Liberation Front. Mexico City became the center of his literary and political activities, with his works translated into multiple languages and influencing audiences worldwide. In 1972, he received the Neustadt International Prize for Literature, and in 1982, the Nobel Prize in Literature.

points.title: 晚年与遗产
points.description: 马尔克斯晚年继续在墨西哥城生活和创作，发表了回忆录《活着为了讲述》和小说《为爱情或其他故事》。他积极参与国际事务，担任联合国教科文组织和平大使，关注拉丁美洲的政治和社会问题。2002年，他被诊断患有淋巴癌，但继续写作直至去世。马尔克斯的文学遗产对世界文学产生了深远影响，魔幻现实主义成为全球文学的重要流派。他的作品被翻译成多种语言，销量超过数千万册，影响了无数作家和读者。2014年4月17日，马尔克斯在墨西哥城去世，享年87岁。
points.descriptionEn: In his later years, García Márquez continued to live and write in Mexico City, publishing the memoir 'Living to Tell the Tale' and the novel 'Memories of My Melancholy Whores.' He actively engaged in international affairs as a UNESCO Goodwill Ambassador, focusing on political and social issues in Latin America. In 2002, he was diagnosed with lymphatic cancer but continued writing until his death. García Márquez's literary legacy has profoundly influenced world literature, with magical realism becoming a significant global literary movement. His works have been translated into numerous languages, selling tens of millions of copies, and influencing countless writers and readers. He died in Mexico City on April 17, 2014, at the age of 87.

supporter.zh: 马尔克斯被誉为20世纪最伟大的作家之一，他的魔幻现实主义风格革新了世界文学。支持者认为他通过《百年孤独》等作品，成功地将拉丁美洲的历史、文化和政治现实呈现给世界，为边缘地区的文学赢得了国际认可。他的叙事技巧和想象力超越了传统现实主义的局限，创造了一个独特的文学宇宙。马尔克斯不仅是一位文学大师，也是拉丁美洲的代言人，他的作品唤起了人们对殖民历史、社会不公和身份认同的深刻思考。
supporter.en: García Márquez is hailed as one of the greatest writers of the 20th century, whose magical realism revolutionized world literature. Supporters argue that through works like 'One Hundred Years of Solitude,' he successfully presented Latin America's history, culture, and political reality to the world, earning international recognition for literature from marginalized regions. His narrative techniques and imagination transcended the limitations of traditional realism, creating a unique literary universe. García Márquez was not only a literary master but also a voice for Latin America, whose works evoke deep reflection on colonial history, social injustice, and identity.

critic.zh: 批评者指出马尔克斯的作品存在政治倾向性，特别是他对左翼政治的支持和对美国政策的批评。一些评论家认为他的魔幻现实主义风格有时过于依赖奇特的情节和夸张的描写，而忽视了文学的现实主义基础。此外，有批评者认为他对女性角色的刻画存在刻板印象，缺乏深度。还有人指出，尽管马尔克斯获得了诺贝尔文学奖，但他的后期作品未能达到早期作品的创新高度，显示出创作力的衰退。
critic.en: Critics point out that García Márquez's works exhibit political bias, particularly his support for left-wing politics and criticism of U.S. policies. Some commentators argue that his magical realism style sometimes relies excessively on peculiar plots and exaggerated descriptions, neglecting the realistic foundations of literature. Additionally, critics note that his portrayal of female characters contains stereotypes and lacks depth. Others suggest that despite his Nobel Prize, his later works failed to reach the innovative heights of his early writings, showing a decline in creative vitality.

objective.zh: 在历史学和流行文化中，马尔克斯被定义为魔幻现实主义的代表人物和拉丁美洲文学爆炸的核心人物。他的作品不仅是文学成就，也是理解拉丁美洲历史和社会的重要窗口。马尔克斯的名字已成为一种文化符号，代表着对传统叙事方式的突破和对边缘声音的肯定。他的作品被广泛纳入世界文学经典，影响了从萨尔曼·拉什迪到村上春树等众多作家。在流行文化中，'马孔多'已成为一个文化原型，象征着拉丁美洲的集体记忆和历史命运。
objective.en: In historical and popular culture contexts, García Márquez is defined as the representative of magical realism and a central figure in the Latin American Boom. His works are not only literary achievements but also important windows for understanding Latin American history and society. García Márquez's name has become a cultural symbol representing breakthroughs in traditional narrative methods and affirmation of marginalized voices. His works are widely included in world literary classics, influencing numerous writers from Salman Rushdie to Haruki Murakami. In popular culture, 'Macondo' has become a cultural prototype symbolizing Latin America's collective memory and historical destiny.

self.zh: 生活不是我们活过的日子，而是我们记住的日子。
self.en: Life is not what one lived, but what one remembers and how one remembers it to tell it.

others.zh: 马尔克斯是拉丁美洲的荷马，他的《百年孤独》是我们时代的《伊利亚特》。
others.en: García Márquez is the Homer of Latin America, and 'One Hundred Years of Solitude' is our 'Iliad'.
